newsitem.title: UK: Heated LME zinc market races ever-higher.
newsitem.headline: Heated LME zinc market races ever-higher.

text.p: Zinc prices continued to race ahead on the London Metal Exchange (LME), notching up yet another 6-3/4 year high on Tuesday, as supply tightness gripped the market, traders said.
Speculative buying lifted three months prices from early little-changed levels of $1,418 a tonne up to $1,442. Meanwhile, the cash/threes contango contracted to just $2/3.
"This market is getting very tight....and there are big players, short and long, gearing up for a fight," one trader said.
Only two weeks ago zinc was trading around $1,350, while the cash/threes contango was a more normal financeable $23/24.
Today's firmer trend was assisted by a 950-tonne drop in LME warehouse stocks, with a net fall in the sensitive Singapore warehouse.
Talk continued to circulate that much of the metal being delivered from China into Singapore is old and of doubtful quality.
On Monday China's Zhuzhou smelter said that Swiss trader Glencore, which had been querying the quality of its 'TORCH' brand, had withdrawn a complaint made to the LME.
Traders said the talk of complaints reflects the battle between major longs and shorts. In the latter case some say there is a large Chinese investment position now some $300 under the market.
"They have been selling zinc for ages - the question is whether they are going to deliver against these shorts," one noted.

There has been a persistent perception that a sizeable tonnage of metal from China will be delivered into Singapore. But its non-appearance in data suggested that the metal is either being held off-warrant or having quality problems.
